page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-8 is a memory-oriented virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. The instance allocates 8 dedicated vCPUs spanning 4 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, backed by 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 33 MB L3 cache. It provides 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding an elevated ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated hardware accelerators, relying on external network-attached volumes for persistent data storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate solid middle-tier performance across memory and system throughput tasks. In memory evaluations, large block uncached read bandwidth reaches 52.02 GB/s, write bandwidth achieves 40.05 GB/s, and Redis SET throughput records 7.13 million operations per second. General compute testing places the system in average performance bands, reflected by a Geekbench multi-core score of 4476 and a PassMark CPU score of 8349.76. However, compute-heavy and vector tasks like ray tracing, image processing, and LLM inference exhibit lower tier efficiency, with 7B model prompt processing achieving 10.36 tokens per second.

The configuration offers balanced resource economics for operations that demand substantial memory capacity without requiring high vCPU counts. Because physical core density is modest at 4 cores, workloads characterized by compute intensity or parallel floating-point calculations will see diminishing returns relative to resource footprint. Instead, the high RAM allocation makes Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-8 suitable for in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, data preprocessing pipelines, and web servers handling high-concurrency memory-resident sessions.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-highmem-8 is a memory-expanded instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.8 GHz and 64.0 GB of RAM. Based on x86_64 architecture with AVX-512 support, it delivers an expanded 8.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. The configuration omits integrated GPUs and bundled local storage, utilizing network storage for persistence. Benchmark evaluation indicates average general-purpose compute and memory performance, evidenced by 52.02 GB/s uncached read bandwidth, a Geekbench multi-core rating of 4476, and 7.13 million Redis SET operations per second. Floating-point and LLM processing benchmarks place in lower percentiles due to core limitations. From an operational efficiency perspective, n2-highmem-8 provides high memory density per core, making it effective for memory-bound tasks including in-memory databases, key-value stores, relational database management systems, and enterprise application servers requiring sizable memory footprints without excess CPU licensing overhead.
